_README: Editorial layer for the 2026 missives. Titles/excerpts/tags are interpretation and are reviewed by a human; the ingest script refuses to invent them. 'trailing' decides what happens to text after the sign-off: 'drop' = drafting residue or ephemeral admin, 'keep' = an intentional postscript. Tags must come from the frozen vocabulary in docs/TAGGING.md or the build fails.

Epiphany of the Lord (transferred).title: Home by Another Way
Epiphany of the Lord (transferred).excerpt: On a song, the magi's detour, and a Spirit who still finds paths around what looks impenetrable.

Baptism of the Lord.title: The Bruised Reed
Baptism of the Lord.excerpt: On a servant who won't snap what is already bent — and the baptismal vows that make that work ours.

2nd Sunday after Epiphany.title: Come and See
2nd Sunday after Epiphany.excerpt: On revelation that arrives by the drip rather than the gallon, and the slow faithfulness of abiding together.

3rd Sunday after Epiphany.title: The Giants of the Pulpit
3rd Sunday after Epiphany.excerpt: On preaching where giants preached, and a God who works through small, bumbling people.

4th Sunday after Epiphany.title: Rebellions of Mercy
4th Sunday after Epiphany.excerpt: On Micah's accusation against the deeply religious and deeply unjust — and why ordinary faithfulness has become an act of rebellion.

5th Sunday after Epiphany.title: The Only Power That Bends
5th Sunday after Epiphany.excerpt: On turning fifty without having learned how to do life, and choosing love when power would be so much easier.

Transfiguration Sunday.title: Forty Days Means a Long Time
Transfiguration Sunday.excerpt: On Torah as gift rather than law, and a transformation that takes a lifetime instead of a moment.

Lent 1.title: Who Told You
Lent 1.excerpt: On fig leaves, the shame that enters and stays, and a God who co-suffers rather than standing apart from our wounds.

Lent 2.title: Songs for the Uphill Road
Lent 2.excerpt: On camp songs, pilgrim psalms, and who keeps us in a wilderness that has no keeper but God.

Lent 3.title: She Is Not One Thing
Lent 3.excerpt: On the woman at the well, the sins we assume she committed, and a gospel that refuses to flatten anyone into a single story.

Lent 4.title: The Brothers Nobody Names
Lent 4.excerpt: On Eliab, the island of misfit toys, and everyone who has been passed over and left unnamed.

Lent 5.title: Preaching to Dry Bones
Lent 5.excerpt: On a drought, a river that stopped running, and the foolishness of speaking life to what is obviously dead.

Palm / Passion Sunday.title: What Jesus Saw from the Donkey
Palm / Passion Sunday.excerpt: On the faces along the parade route, and a shout of Hosanna already shadowed by another cry.

Easter Sunday.title: Dew Still on the Roses
Easter Sunday.excerpt: On arriving at the garden exhausted, being called by name, and the gift of an Easter afternoon nap.

Easter 2.title: What Thomas Touched
Easter 2.excerpt: On whether they were scars or still open wounds — and a resurrection that transforms suffering without erasing it.

Easter 3.title: Three Thousand in a Day
Easter 3.excerpt: On Acts as a window rather than a blueprint, and the honest question of whether you are carrying more than you were meant to carry alone.

Easter 4.title: The Plastic-Covered Psalm
Easter 4.excerpt: On a psalm we save for funerals the way a grandmother saves a couch under plastic — and the rest we refuse ourselves.
Easter 4._note: SUPERSEDED? The Drive folder holds a second Easter 4 doc marked 'replacement' — the guest letter from Lisa Straus. Held as a draft on the assumption the guest letter went out in this slot instead. Confirm with Celia whether this Psalm 23 letter was ever sent.

easter 4 -- replacement.title: Seventy Years of Full Clergy Rights
easter 4 -- replacement.excerpt: A guest letter marking the 1956 decision that opened ordination to women — and a call to male colleagues to say so out loud.
easter 4 -- replacement.author: Lisa Straus
easter 4 -- replacement._note: Not by Celia — signed 'Lisa Straus, Senior Pastor Tarrytown UMC'. No liturgical-day header and no epigraph block; Galatians 3:28 is quoted inline and is recorded as the epigraph because it is the verse the letter hangs on. Points to GCSRW resources for Pentecost (May 24), which is why it likely went out a month ahead, in the Easter 4 slot.

Easter 5.title: How Can We Know the Way
Easter 5.excerpt: On Thomas the practical and the needy — snarky, sarcastic, and brave enough to ask for what he needed when he needed it.
Easter 5._note: The Drive doc contains TWO drafts of this letter — a polished version, then an earlier rough draft pasted below the sign-off, then a stray closing paragraph. Only the polished version is imported.

Easter 6.title: Functional Atheism
Easter 6.excerpt: On leading as though everything depends on you, and a promise that you will not be left orphaned.
Easter 6._note: CITATION FIX: the Drive doc cites the epigraph as John 14:8, but the quoted words ('I will not leave you orphaned; I am coming to you') are John 14:18. Recorded as 14:18. Worth telling Celia — it went out with the wrong verse number.

Easter 7.title: Never Quite Prepared
Easter 7.excerpt: On years of having seen some things, a Spirit entirely beyond our control, and how little any of it prepares us.

Pentecost.title: That Pesky Holy Spirit
Pentecost.excerpt: On a Spirit who is not a labor-saving device, tiny Pentecosts, and sparks that refuse to stay inside the plan.

Trinity sunday.title: Not Fully Myself Without You
Trinity sunday.excerpt: On skipping the doctrinal sermon and asking instead what it means that none of us carries the image of God alone.

2nd post pentecost.title: The Company Jesus Keeps
2nd post pentecost.excerpt: On sin and sickness as forms of separation, and a physician determined to cross every barrier we build.

3 post Pentecost.title: Take No Bag for the Journey
3 post Pentecost.excerpt: On evangelism with empty hands, elaborate travel plans, and a Holy Spirit with a well-documented sense of humor.
3 post Pentecost._note: The postscript below the sign-off is INTENTIONAL — she wrote the letter before her Pittsburgh trip and added the (disastrous) outcome afterward. It is the punchline. Do not cut it.

8th post pentecost.title: Surely the Lord Is in This Place
8th post pentecost.excerpt: On Jacob's rock pillow, a parishioner in the emergency room, and why we are still surprised when God shows up.
8th post pentecost._note: The closing paragraph on Jacob as an unreliable narrator sits below the sign-off but is addressed to readers and trails into the next letters on Jacob. Kept as a postscript.

9th post pentecost.title: A Kingdom You Cannot Own
9th post pentecost.excerpt: On buried treasure, invasive weeds, and a kingdom that arrives whether or not we are ready for it.

10th post pentecost.title: Say Your Name
10th post pentecost.excerpt: On a grabby, conniving scoundrel forced to say his own name out loud — and a God who still will not let go.

11th post pentecost.title: Ego Eimi
11th post pentecost.excerpt: On translating when nobody asked you to, and finding 'I am' in the middle of the storm.

12th Post pentecost.title: What Came Out of His Mouth
12th Post pentecost.excerpt: On the hardest thing to say about this text — that our savior insults a foreigner, and is redeemed by her faith.

13th Post Pentecost.title: Shiphrah and Puah
13th Post Pentecost.excerpt: On midwives who turned the oppressor's own contempt into a tool of resistance — and whether we are willing to learn how.

14th post pentecost.title: Turning Aside
14th post pentecost.excerpt: On Moses and the sheep, the numbing routine of the work, and how many burning bushes we walk straight past.

15th Post Pentecost.title: Where Two or Three Are Gathered
15th Post Pentecost.excerpt: On a verse we quote to excuse a thin crowd, and the church conflict it was actually about.
